name: capability-placement-sweep-synthetic
note: SYNTHETIC corpus for #54. 20 fresh, confirmed-unimplemented tasks (verified absent from master at freeze) graded easy/medium/hard. Chosen over closed-ticket replay because replaying shipped tickets against current master is base-contaminated (the solution already exists → accept-rate uninformative). Tradeoff: no known-good shipped reference; accept-rate is judged on the replayed PR (tests pass + human).
inject: File each as an issue, assignee=Jesuso, label=agent:triage (fail-closed: no assignee OR no source label = no fire). Set the config tiering BEFORE injecting each config run.

tasks.title: doctor: warn when maxConcurrent is unset or < 1
tasks.why: One validation branch + message in doctor.js.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`doctor` should flag a `queue.maxConcurrent` that is missing or `< 1` (would stall the queue).

## Acceptance
- With `maxConcurrent` unset or `<1`, `doctor` prints a WARN line naming the field and the effective default.
- With a valid value, no new output.
- Covered by a unit test.

tasks.title: cleanup: report total disk reclaimed
tasks.why: Sum sizes + one summary line; localized to cleanup.js.
tasks.body:
## Goal
After `cleanup --apply`, print how much disk the removed worktrees reclaimed.

## Acceptance
- Summary line like `reclaimed 42.3 MB across 3 worktrees`.
- `--apply` absent (dry) prints the would-reclaim total instead.
- No change to what gets removed.

tasks.title: ah usage: --since <duration> window filter
tasks.why: New flag parsed to a cutoff; filter the usage rows.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`ah usage --since 24h` (also `7d`, `90m`) limits the summary to runs newer than the cutoff.

## Acceptance
- Accepts `Nh`/`Nd`/`Nm`; rejects garbage with a clear error.
- Rows older than the cutoff are excluded from totals.
- Composes with existing `--day`/`--week`.

tasks.title: reconcile: --dry-run lists without dispatching
tasks.why: Guard the dispatch call behind a flag; print the plan.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`reconcile --dry-run` prints the tasks it WOULD replay (ref + step) and dispatches nothing.

## Acceptance
- No `claude -p` spawned, no board writes under `--dry-run`.
- Output lists each resting task and its target step.
- Normal `reconcile` unchanged.

tasks.title: config: ${VAR:-default} fallback in interpolation
tasks.why: Extend the ${VAR} regex/replacer in config.js.
tasks.body:
## Goal
Config interpolation should support `${VAR:-default}` — use `default` when `VAR` is unset/empty.

## Acceptance
- `${PORT:-4123}` yields `4123` when `PORT` unset, else `$PORT`.
- Plain `${VAR}` behavior unchanged (still errors/blank per current rule).
- Unit test over the interpolation function.

tasks.title: follow: --lines N controls initial tail size
tasks.why: Add a flag; pass N to the initial read.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`follow --lines 200` sets how many trailing lines print before live-tailing (current fixed default stays the default).

## Acceptance
- `--lines N` respected; non-numeric → clear error.
- Live tail after the initial dump is unchanged.

tasks.title: catchup: accept multiple refs in one call
tasks.why: Loop the existing single-ref path over argv.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`catchup <refA> <refB> ...` replays several refs in one invocation.

## Acceptance
- Each ref runs the existing single-ref logic; a bad ref is reported and skipped, others proceed.
- Exit non-zero only if every ref failed.
- Single-ref behavior identical to today.

tasks.title: ah logs <ref>: print per-run log paths for a ref
tasks.why: New command reusing sessions.js run-log correlation.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`ah logs <ref>` prints the per-run log file path(s) for a task ref, most-recent last.

## Acceptance
- Resolves the ref via the same mapping `resume`/`follow` use.
- One path per line; `--json` optional.
- Unknown ref → clear error, non-zero exit.

tasks.title: status: per-step success/fail/changes counts
tasks.why: Aggregate the per-run logs by step; render a small table.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`status` gains a per-step outcome tally (success / fail / changes) derived from the run logs.

## Acceptance
- Counts come from actual run-log verdicts, not guesses.
- Renders under the existing status output; empty history → zeros, no crash.
- Aggregation covered by a unit test with fixture logs.

tasks.title: dispatch: per-step maxRuntime timeout kills hung claude -p
tasks.why: Timer around the spawn; SIGTERM then SIGKILL; verdict=fail.
tasks.body:
## Goal
Add an optional per-step `maxRuntime` (seconds). A `claude -p` exceeding it is terminated and the run resolved as `fail`.

## Acceptance
- Timeout → SIGTERM, escalate to SIGKILL after a grace window; run recorded `fail` with a timeout reason.
- Unset `maxRuntime` = no timeout (today's behavior).
- The kill path does not leak the child or its worktree lock.

tasks.title: trackers: retry advance with bounded backoff on transient 5xx
tasks.why: Wrap the advance HTTP call in a small retry helper.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`advance` should retry on transient 5xx / network errors with bounded exponential backoff instead of failing the move immediately.

## Acceptance
- Max N attempts, capped backoff, jitter; 4xx is NOT retried.
- Exhausted retries → the same failure surface as today.
- Helper unit-tested with a fake failing-then-succeeding call.

tasks.title: emit structured events.jsonl audit log per profile
tasks.why: Append-only JSONL on enqueue/dispatch/advance/fail.
tasks.body:
## Goal
Write one JSON line per lifecycle event (enqueue, dispatch, advance, fail) to `events.jsonl` in the profile state dir.

## Acceptance
- Each line: `{ts, event, ref, step, ...}`; append-only, never rewritten.
- Failure to write the log never breaks the pipeline (best-effort).
- Documented field set.

tasks.title: reconcile: --step <id> replays only one step by id
tasks.why: Filter listResting output by step before dispatch.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`reconcile --step code` replays only tasks resting in that step's source stage.

## Acceptance
- Unknown step id → clear error listing valid ids.
- Without `--step`, behavior unchanged.
- Composes with `--dry-run` (E4) if present.

tasks.title: agents: elapsed-runtime column per claude -p
tasks.why: Derive start time from proc/logs; render a duration column.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`ah agents` shows how long each running `claude -p` has been alive.

## Acceptance
- Human duration (e.g. `3m12s`) per row, sorted stable with existing columns.
- No new false-positive process matches (respect the existing match tightening).
- Degrades gracefully when start time is unknown.

tasks.title: stop: --drain lets in-flight runs finish before exit
tasks.why: Stop intake, await queue idle, then shut down.
tasks.body:
## Goal
`stop --drain` stops accepting new webhook events but waits for active runs to finish before terminating (bounded by an optional timeout).

## Acceptance
- No new jobs dispatched after `--drain` begins.
- Exits once the queue is idle or the timeout elapses (then force-stop, logged).
- Plain `stop` behavior unchanged.

tasks.title: Slack notifier: POST to a webhook on run start/finish/fail
tasks.why: New optional, config-gated side-channel wired into dispatch.
tasks.body:
## Goal
An optional Slack notifier posts to a configured incoming-webhook URL on run start, success, and failure.

## Acceptance
- Config-gated (absent config = feature off, zero behavior change).
- Non-blocking + best-effort: a Slack failure never affects the pipeline outcome.
- Message includes ref, step, outcome, and a link/id. Documented config key.

tasks.title: Linear tracker adapter
tasks.why: Full new adapter mirroring the asana.js interface.
tasks.body:
## Goal
Add a `linear` tracker adapter implementing the full adapter contract (see the asana.js header doc-comment): describe, authenticate, processEvents, fetchTask, advance, listResting, registerWebhook, unregisterWebhooks, forgeCatchup, and wizardSteps.

## Acceptance
- Registered in `src/trackers/index.js` under `type: "linear"`.
- Steps bind Linear workflow states; `advance` moves an issue between states.
- Passes `npm run typecheck`; contract-style tests mirror `test/github.test.js`.
- Setup doc under `docs/`.

tasks.title: config hot-reload on SIGHUP (no in-flight drop)
tasks.why: Re-read pipeline on signal; swap config without losing running jobs.
tasks.body:
## Goal
On `SIGHUP`, the running server re-reads its config (pipeline steps, tiering) and applies it to NEW jobs without dropping in-flight runs.

## Acceptance
- In-flight jobs keep the config they started with; new jobs use the reloaded config.
- Invalid reloaded config is rejected and the old config stays live (logged).
- No listener/webhook churn on reload.

tasks.title: read-only web status page at GET /status
tasks.why: New server route rendering heartbeat + queue as HTML.
tasks.body:
## Goal
Serve a read-only HTML status page at `GET /status`: profile, url, queue depth, active agents, recent runs — from the existing heartbeat/state.

## Acceptance
- GET only; no state mutation; safe to expose read-only.
- Does not interfere with webhook POST routing or the fast-ACK path.
- Renders with zero in-flight runs (empty state) without error.

tasks.title: auto model-escalation on changes-loop exhaustion
tasks.why: Extend #53 semantics: escalate a tier before final fail.
tasks.body:
## Goal
When a `(ref,step)` hits `maxAttempts` on the `changes` loop, retry ONCE at the next model/effort tier before resolving `fail`.

## Acceptance
- The escalated retry is recorded distinctly in attempts/usage (not an infinite loop).
- No escalation configured / no higher tier available → today's fail behavior.
- The per-`(ref,step)` cap still bounds total work.
